geological-processes.sourceSummary: Earthquake shaking can affect buildings and trigger slope movement; landslides can alter streams and vegetation. Volcanic material weathering can eventually support fertile soil and volcanic heat can be used as a resource.
geological-processes.attributionLimits: Actual general accounts and named1958 Lituya Bay environmental example remain distinct from the following original fictional town scenario. No images, local risk calculation, predicted event or death tally.
geological-processes.question: Original town case: supplied facts state that underground slip shakes two areas with different ground/building conditions; a triggered slide moves soil/vegetation and blocks a stream beside a road. Analyse the cause→physical change→environmental and social consequences, including possible downstream flooding and road/service disruption. Contrast immediate effects with the source-described long-term benefit of weathered volcanic material; explain the timescale difference.
geological-processes.expectedEvidence: Separate underground cause, shaking, land/water change and effects on people. Explain why geology, exposure and building design matter; connect stream/vegetation change to a possible habitat consequence without inventing a measured population loss. Explain weathering/soil benefit as a long-term possibility, not every eruption being good.
geological-processes.nearMiss: Describes only ground shaking or only a protective device, says all buildings respond equally or that fertile soils make an active eruption safe.
geological-processes.changedCase: Original change: the same slip occurs farther from buildings and with a slope that does not fail. Revise which consequences follow; identify which supplied facts/evidence would be needed before claiming a blocked stream or community harm.

aluminium-life.sourceSummary: Bauxite is refined to alumina, then aluminium metal is manufactured/shaped into products; production uses energy and generates residues. Collected aluminium can be remelted, while material discarded in general waste may not return to production.
aluminium-life.attributionLimits: Original one-product pathway. A general source does not establish a current mine's compliance, every municipality's collection rules or exact lifecycle totals. No industrial/chemical demonstration.
aluminium-life.question: Original prepared pathway: bauxite extraction → alumina refining → aluminium production and shaping → useful drink container → collection/sorting/remelting into another product OR disposal. For each stage identify the resource transformation, a supported environmental effect/question and social use, burden or decision. Compare original fictional perspectives of a production worker concerned with useful work/safe jobs, a nearby resident concerned with residue/water protection, a container user and a recycling operator needing clean separated material. Propose an avoid/reuse/collect/recycle response and explain what it changes and leaves unresolved.
aluminium-life.expectedEvidence: Cover ALL five source stages: extraction, refining, manufacturing, recycling and disposal, not just the final bin. Link energy/material/residue evidence to environmental concerns and useful packaging/handling/infrastructure needs to social impacts. Compare perspectives and justify a bounded recommendation; recycling can reduce new extraction/production demand but still requires collection/energy and does not erase all earlier impacts.
aluminium-life.nearMiss: Says recycling cleans all mine waste, equates refining with shaping a can, treats every thrown-away can as recycled or substitutes a mineral name for the lifecycle assessment.
aluminium-life.changedCase: Original change: a town cannot currently collect the selected container, while another has a verified collection route. Explain how recommendations and required information differ, without asserting the worked foreign collection advice is a local rule or asking a child to handle waste.
